::: {.callout-important title="The association is descriptive and exploratory"}
The within-understood association $\psi$ (and therefore the data-identified $p_{\text{any}}$) rests on the ~60 uk\_02 four-cell rows (~34 children, ≈19–56 months). It is a single scalar — the data do not support an age-varying association at this sample size — and is **descriptive / exploratory**. The four-cell composition and $p_{\text{any}}$ outside that age window lean on the marginal trajectories plus scalar-$\psi$ extrapolation. Signing data exist only for the Down syndrome datasets, so there is no typically-developing comparison.

At this sample size a point estimate that clears the independence reference $\psi = 1$ is, on average, inflated in magnitude — the Type-M ("winner's-curse") consequence of selecting on a noisy quantity — so the credible interval and the strength of evidence, not the point value of $\psi$, should carry the interpretation.
:::
